_comment: The canonical skeleton. Every plan starts here. This file does not validate on purpose: the required fields are absent because they are yours to fill in. Delete this comment and the ones below as you go.
_goal: One sentence saying what done looks like. Not what to do - what will be true afterwards.
_project: Either { "id": "<uuid of an existing project>" } or { "name": "my-project" } to create one. A new project gets a Gitea repository.
_assumptions: At least one. Everything the plan rests on that could turn out to be false. Say how confident you are and what breaks if you are wrong - the operator reads these at the gate and this is where a bad plan gets caught.
_non_goals: What this plan will NOT do. The schema allows an empty list; do not leave it empty. This is the only thing stopping the agent widening its own scope.
_env: "dev" or "prod". Selects which worker VM runs the whole plan.
_tasks: The DAG. Small tasks with small feedback loops: each one produces something checkable before the next depends on it. Size limits to what the task needs, not to the maximum.
_success_criteria: How the orchestrator decides the plan worked. Only two kinds exist: { "type": "all_tasks_done" } and { "type": "file_exists_in_branch", "path": "..." }. Anything else has to become a file the plan produces.
_egress: Hostnames the sandboxes may reach, on top of Gitea and the package registries. Deny-by-default: a host not listed here fails at the proxy. "*.example.com" is allowed and does not match the apex.
_max_tokens: The whole plan's token ceiling, across every task and every attempt. Omitting it means the sum of the task ceilings, which is generous - name a real number.
_env_ttl_min: How long the environment lives before it is torn down. Default 240.

_task_shape.description: Plain text. Everything the agent needs to do this one task, including any rollback note if it touches something outside the plan branch.
depends_on: ids of tasks that must finish first
_task_shape.failure_policy: { "type": "halt" } or { "type": "retry", "max_attempts": 1-5 }. halt is the default and is right for most things; retry is for genuine flakiness, never for a task that failed because it was wrong.
